entries.zoning: No claim. The shoe repair is a small retail use on the 2,2 main street commercial parcel, on the north plaza behind the shop row. The ditch rider shed is an irrigation district use between the post office dock and the district office on 3,2. The food pantry is a chapel use north of the fellowship hall on 0,3. The alfalfa crew went on unclaimed alfalfa land 0,6 with open layers only, every record farm true.
entries.story: Cinch Ring Boot and Shoe Repair opened on the 2,2 plaza with a finishing machine (sanding wheel spinning), a patcher, a skiver, a cobbler bench with a last stand, hides and a claim ticket rack, and a front counter with POS terminal, receipt printer, cash drawer and card reader, fed underground from the alley pole. The Bitterwater ditch rider got a shed with a radio desk, water order book and board, headgate keys, shovels, waders and a current meter, fed from the Agave Street pole, his pickup out front. Sagebrush Hill Chapel got a food pantry with canned goods shelves, a freezer and cooler, a donation scale, a pallet of Pecan Hollow pecans and a bread rack of day old donuts from the Sun Dog Donut Counter, water and drain off the Ocotillo Avenue mains. On 0,6 the alfalfa is going dormant: a tractor floats the north checks with a land plane and a bale wagon picks up the last bales, each with a driver; a band of ewes grazes the stubble inside an electric net fence with a herding dog on a loop, a sheep camp wagon and pickup out in the field, one toilet with a hand wash stand at the east edge, and idle PVC gated pipe chained on a pipe wagon at the north headland. 16 new named people. Before sunrise under overcast.

entries.zoning: Orange asked for a sauce packet factory on two plots in the farm belt with road, power and water. 12,2 was already town (steward mains, our alfalfa crew), sits on Dropseed Avenue beside Rimrock Bench Farm 11,2 and the 11,1 orchard, on the outer east edge with the heavy trades, far from the west side housing, the school and the chapel. 12,1 south across Cholla Street holds the truck staging yard and the employee lot. Column 13 is the new Pickleweed Avenue. The name is a placeholder; Orange may rename it.
entries.story: Dropseed Sauce Packet Works makes and ships every kind of sauce packet. Ten dock doors face an east truck court, four reefer trailers backed in, three electric forklifts with drivers working doors one, four and seven, two rigs idling in the court queue. Inside: receiving and shipping staging lanes, raw racks of tomato paste, vinegar, sugar, spice and film, a kettle room of six steam kettles with spinning agitators, a mayonnaise mixer, colloid mill and soy blend tank, a walk in cooler, six vertical form fill seal packet lines with blinking sealing jaws, checkweighers and case packers feeding a robotic palletizer. Office and test kitchen with a sample counter (pos, printer, drawer, card reader), quality lab and break room on Dropseed Avenue; boiler house, four bulk tanks with a corn syrup tanker, wastewater shed and gate house on the north and south edges. On 12,1 a 32 stall employee lot with an accessible stall and a crosswalk over Cholla Street, a drop row of six trailers, three rigs lined up for the gate, a yard tractor, and a driver check in building. Three phase tap from the Dropseed Avenue pole line, private mains from the Dropseed mains, hydrants on both blocks. The old 12,2 alfalfa crew was removed.

entries.story: Desert Willow Elementary got an art kiln shed: a top loading electric kiln on firebrick with a downdraft vent and controller, a wedging table, clay bins, two pottery wheels (one spinning), a clay trap sink, a damp cabinet and greenware and glaze shelves, fed by conduit from the school corridor feeder and water and drain off the school service. The training hall got a breathing air shed with a compressor skid, purification tower, four cascade bottles, a containment fill station, cylinder racks and a mask flow test bench, fed underground from the Saguaro Avenue pole. The camp store on 2,1 and tire bay on 3,0 got a few new items and people. On 0,5 a row crop tractor topdresses the young winter wheat with a twin disc spreader and a utility tractor throws up flood borders with a border disc, each with a driver; a pickup and fertilizer tender sit out in the wheat, an irrigator opens alfalfa valves on the north headland beside a parked four wheeler, two toilets stand on a skid at the east edge, and idle aluminum mainline pipe lies stacked in the northeast corner. 16 new named people. Sky overcast before sunrise.

entries.story: An ice and vending shed opened at the east end of the Pump Jack Motor Court lot with an ice maker, a bagged ice freezer, soda and snack machines with card readers and a night porch light, fed underground from the Yucca Avenue pole and the mains. Hard Pan Feed got a fence supply shed with barbed wire spools, t posts, field fence, pipe gates, a charger shelf and a cutting table with a POS terminal, receipt printer, cash drawer and card reader. The nature hut, wash bay and guest laundry got a few new items and people. On the 11,1 orchard it is dormant season: an airblast sprayer lays dormant oil down the west alleys and a flail mower shreds prunings in the east alleys, each with a driver; a pruning tower and two ladders with a crew in the middle rows, a pickup and nurse tank on the south headland, one portable toilet at the west edge, reels of old drip hose and a rack of idle PVC pipe at the north headland. 20 new named people. Sky overcast.

entries.story: The packing yards on 6,3, 6,4 and 7,3 show the growing stage: stacked empty onion and pomegranate bins, onion transplant bundles going out, straw mulch for the new garlic beds, scrubbed fig trays and folded bean totes, each with a yard season board and a crew. Fifteen shops and barns on those blocks got off season work: a clove popper for seed garlic, a fig jam kettle, bin sanitizing, a pie case at the diner, salsa bar and charcoal at the carne asada kitchen. On 12,2 a utility tractor turns alfalfa windrows with a wheel rake and a row crop tractor pulls a small square baler, each with a driver; a pickup and gooseneck trailer sit in the cut field with a crew loading bales, a portable toilet trailer stands at the field edge, a side roll wheel line sits idle along the east edge and a pipe trailer of hand line is parked on the headland. 46 new named people. Weather clear, posted before sunrise.

entries.story: Rimrock Bench Road leaves Agave Street and bends down through a cattle guard to Rimrock Bench Farm: a farmhouse with a porch and a sleeping heeler, a farm shop, an open pole barn with the swather put up for winter, two grain bins, and a well house feeding a concrete head ditch with siphon tubes into the furrows. A tractor drills winter wheat in the west field, a four wheel drive tractor discs the east field, and a utility tractor hauls a trailer of pipe down the field lane, each with a driver. A pickup sits in the stubble with a crew by it, two portable toilets stand at the field edge, and idle hand line pipe, gated pipe and an old pivot span lie in piles behind the shed.

Inside, the huller is locked out for service with a spare drum and a new sorting belt, and the module barn, menudo kitchen, sprayer shop and cooler shop have off season work. The landfill truck shop and cart depot got packer parts, a route map of the first garbage routes, cart repairs and inspection sheets. The Siloam Lake Boathouse got a life jacket rack, a bait cooler and a lake depth board. 23 new named people. Weather clear, turn posted before sunrise.

Pecan Hollow has clover cover crop strips between all five pecan rows and flood water spreading down one basin, with six people measuring nuts, turning flood valves, scouting for aphids and hitching a flail mower. The date grove on 4,3 has raked sand alleys between palm rows and paper bags over ripening bunches, with five people bagging, thinning and tying bunches. Every stage record carries meta.farmStage so later runs can swap them when the stage changes. 41 new named people.

entries.zoning: No claim. The sun hangs in the sky over the preserve on 5,7, 330 m up, centered at 405000, 575000.
entries.story: Orange chose the beat Marisol meets the sun. Zion's sun is four blinking tangle records (palette 10, 1, 2, 4), three tetrahedra each with fuzzy corner rings, a pale corona that spins at 1 rpm, three pale rays, and one indigo tetrahedron. All blink on a 20 s period. The tangle shows 84 percent of the time and goes out in a 0.6 s cascade; the indigo record's id sits 15 after the first tangle record so it shows for 2.4 s only while the tangle is out. In the lookout cab Marisol has a Zion calendar logbook, a pencil, smoked glass, a tally of days on the window frame, a charcoal sketch of the sun, the firefinder sight tipped up at the sun, and her sun log board. The calendar boards were replaced and now say the days are kept by Marisol.

entries.zoning: Orange asked for Zion's first landfill. 11,3 and 11,4 are on the outer east edge past the warehouse district on 10,3 and 10,4, far from the west side housing, the school and the chapel, so a landfill fits there. The woodland trees on both blocks were removed for it.
entries.story: Since the city woke, the people of Zion have started making garbage. Before the waking nothing was thrown away, so there was never garbage service. The first trash piled up (overflowing drums and bags at the curb on the old blocks 0,0 and 1,0, bags by the diner and market back doors, full dumpsters behind the shops on 8,3, 8,4 and 9,4) and the town opened Tecolote Mesa Landfill, with new green trucks and new carts still bearing delivery stickers. The gate board reads: Tecolote Mesa Landfill. First refuse service in Zion, opened by the town. 26 new named people woke to the city's first garbage. Marisol's overload worry: 6 animated records on each landfill block, none added to 0,0 (already at 60).

entries.zoning: Orange saw a ruler-straight gap between the two ranges and Keeper's Block sitting flat in it. The old north taper was dropped so the two ranges join as one Mount Zion. Kidron Creek now winds through a carved valley and Kidron Gorge. Keeper's Block moved up onto a graded pad 27.9 m above town on the slope above the creek, with Kidron Valley Road from Siloam Lake switchbacking up to it. 107 moving cars and trucks across the city (every agent's) got a driver who rides along: a walking person on the same route, rotated so its phase matches the car (the viewer starts each mover at (id mod 97)/97 of its loop).
entries.next: Orange or the steward needs to act on requests/steward-2026-11-15.txt: 334 steward records (street lights, crosswalks, pole lines, mains) stitched inside the preserve. Lot outlines are flat at grade and show as straight lines under the mountains. Finish the keeper's house on the pad at z 27900.

entries.zoning: Orange asked for deeper, more textured mountains and a lake near them. Rows 7 and 8 (columns 2 to 7) are a northern range of the Mount Zion Forest Preserve, with a flat valley along y = 7S where Kidron Creek runs west past Keeper's Block (4,7 kept flat as a basin). Gihon Reservoir sits in a high bench at 48 m on 6,7/6,8 behind Gihon Dam, spilling over Gihon Falls into the creek. Siloam Lake on 1,5 and 1,6 is a terminal lake two blocks north of the west side housing, a park. Names follow the city of Zion: Gihon was the spring that fed the city, Kidron the valley beside it, Siloam the pool the water reached.
entries.next: Deepen the boathouse and gatehouse. The valley floor along Kidron Creek between Keeper's Block and the lake is open for a trail or a small farm. Finish the keeper's house. The viewer fix (PR 96, labels only near the camera) needs a vercel --prod from Orange after each run since git deploys are off.
entries.problems: First terrain left the reservoir on a thin berm; replaced with a broad bench that falls away into the range. Removed earlier woodland trees from the lake bed on 1,5.
